definition_law: A person whose application was complete and actionable (fee paid or waived, if any) and who was notified of admission, denial, a place on the waiting list, or withdrew. Same as CDS applicant, applied to the JD program.
definition_ug: An individual who has fulfilled your requirements to be considered for admission (including payment or waiving of the application fee, if any) and who has been notified of admission, nonadmission, placement on the waiting list, or application withdrawn.

definition_law: Offered admission to the JD program, including a person admitted from the waiting list. The offer date is the date the offer was communicated.
definition_ug: Offered admission to a degree-granting program, including a person admitted from the waiting list. The offer date is the date the offer was communicated.

definition_law: Enrolled at the official census date of the entry term. Please use one definition for all years. It should reconcile to the matriculants you report to the ABA.
definition_ug: Enrolled at the official census date of the entry term. Please use one definition for all years. It should reconcile to enrolled first-time first-year students in your Common Data Set (C1).

definition_law: First-year JD entrant, or transfer JD entrant (enters the second year or later from another JD program). Visiting and non-JD students are excluded.
definition_ug: First-time, first-year: attending any institution for the first time at the undergraduate level (including students who first attended in the prior summer, and those with college credit earned before high school graduation). Transfer: entering for the first time but known to have attended another postsecondary institution at the same level.

definition_law: As defined in the ABA Standard 509 report for your program.
definition_ug: Full-time: 12 or more semester or quarter credits per term. Part-time: fewer.

definition_law: Residency of the applicant at application, from the known physical address at the time of application: resident or nonresident of your state, or international. If your ABA filing uses a different basis, tell us. Billing residency, if different, goes in `tuition_residency`.
definition_ug: In-state, out-of-state, international or unknown, from the known physical address at the time of application (CDS C1). Billing residency, if different, goes in `tuition_residency`.

definition_law: Binding early decision, if offered; otherwise regular or rolling.
definition_ug: Early decision (binding; the applicant agrees to enroll if admitted and to withdraw other applications), early action (non-binding), restrictive early action, regular, rolling.

definition_law: Applicants who meet the admission requirements but are offered a place only if space becomes available. Send the date placed and, if later admitted, the offer date.
definition_ug: Students who meet the admission requirements but are offered a place only if space becomes available. Send the date placed and, if later admitted, the offer date.

definition_law: Admitted applicants allowed to postpone enrollment. Send the cohort and term in which the student actually entered.
definition_ug: Admitted students allowed to postpone enrollment, usually one term or one year. Send the cohort and term in which the student actually entered.

definition_law: What the student was told, on the offer date. For Tier 2, keep every package version, not only the final one.
definition_ug: What the student was told, on the offer date. For Tier 2, keep every package version, not only the final one.

definition_law: The student's deposit deadline or the date the student deposited, whichever is earlier. Awards that arrive later (for example, external scholarships reported after enrollment) must carry their true dates so we can keep them out of the price analysis.
definition_ug: The student's deposit deadline or the date the student deposited, whichever is earlier. Awards that arrive later (for example, external scholarships reported after enrollment) must carry their true dates so we can keep them out of the price analysis.

definition_law: Every award revision carries one reason: student request, documented competing offer, staff-initiated, or appeal.
definition_ug: Every award revision carries one reason: student request, documented competing offer, staff-initiated, or appeal.

definition_law: Need-based: awarded only to students who demonstrate financial need. Non-need-based: awarded on merit or any other non-need reason. We classify each fund by its own rule.
definition_ug: Need-based scholarship or grant aid: from institutional, state, federal or other sources, for which a student must have financial need to qualify. Non-need-based: awarded solely on academic achievement, merit or any other non-need reason. We classify each fund by its own rule, not by the CDS precedence order for counting non-need aid used to meet need.

definition_law: Endowed scholarships, annual gifts and tuition-funded grants for which you determine the recipient.
definition_ug: Endowed scholarships, annual gifts and tuition-funded grants for which you determine the recipient.

definition_law: Scholarships and grants from outside sources that students bring with them. You may process the paperwork, but you do not decide the recipient or the amount.
definition_ug: Scholarships and grants from outside sources that students bring with them (for example, National Merit). You may process the paperwork, but you do not decide the recipient or the amount.

definition_law: Report waivers and remission as their own component, not inside institutional merit.
definition_ug: Report waivers as their own component, not inside institutional merit. They are an excluded group.

definition_law: Federal and state work-study aid, and any employment packaged by your institution.
definition_ug: Federal and state work-study aid, and any employment packaged by your institution.

definition_law: Any applicant who submits any institutionally required aid application, such as the FAFSA.
definition_ug: Any applicant who submits any institutionally required aid application, such as the FAFSA.

definition_law: EFC for aid years through 2023-24 and SAI for 2024-25 onward, with a column saying which. Keep negative SAI values. Send it only if need is part of your scholarship decisions or loan-eligibility analysis.
definition_ug: EFC for aid years through 2023-24 and SAI for 2024-25 onward, with a column saying which. Keep negative SAI values. 'No FAFSA' is its own category.

definition_law: Tuition, required fees (those every full-time student pays), and the housing and food, books and personal budget you use for packaging.
definition_ug: Tuition, required fees (those every full-time student pays), food and housing (double occupancy, 19 meals a week or the maximum plan), books and supplies, and transportation (two round trips home for students in institutional housing).

definition_law: A person whose first recorded contact is the application. Flag them; do not drop them.
definition_ug: A person whose first recorded contact is the application. Flag them; do not drop them.

definition_law: Send the raw score and the test type. Leave blank if not submitted. Do not impute or convert. State whether the LSAT score is the highest or the average, and who calculated UGPA (LSAC or the school).
definition_ug: Leave blank if not submitted. Do not impute or convert.

definition_law: Missing is never zero. Leave unknown values blank. If aid data does not exist for a cohort, tell us instead of sending zeros.
definition_ug: Missing is never zero. Leave unknown values blank. If aid data does not exist for a cohort, tell us instead of sending zeros.

definition_law: Send your raw source strings. We apply a versioned mapping and return a list of anything unmapped for your review.
definition_ug: Send your raw source strings. We apply a versioned mapping and return a list of anything unmapped for your review.
